data.title: CSE Bulletin: New Listing - Peptide Development Labs Inc. (PEPT)
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - The common shares of Peptide Development Labs Inc. have been approved for listing on the CSE.

Listing and disclosure documents will be available at www.thecse.com on the listing date.

Peptide Development Labs Inc. is a Canadian pharmaceutical development company focused on advancing investigational peptide-based drug candidates through established regulatory pathways. The Issuer’s mission is to develop peptide candidates that may address defined areas of unmet clinical need within a conventional pharmaceutical framework. To achieve this, the Issuer focuses on advancing its investigational subcutaneous BPC-157 drug candidate for refractory ligament disorders through GMP-controlled supply, pharmaceutical quality systems, physician-led access, structured data generation and formal clinical development.

data.title: Gold extends losses below $3,700, pressured by rate-hike bets
data.description:
Gold futures fell for the sixth time in eight sessions to fresh 14-month lows on Thursday, as the market's overwhelming consensus anticipates a rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December meeting to combat stubborn inflation.

Minutes from last month's FOMC meeting showed nearly all Fed officials expected interest ​rates will need to move higher, reinforcing sentiments expressed ‌by ⁠several policymakers during the week, including Fed Governor Christopher Waller, who said the central bank may need to respond more aggressively to rising prices.

Traders now see a 94% probability of a 25-bp interest rate boost next month, according to the CME's FedWatch tool, and the dollar index this week reached ​its highest level in 19 months, making dollar-priced gold more expensive for overseas buyers.

Gold prices could fall to $3,500/oz as expectations of interest rate hikes drive bond yields higher and support U.S. dollar strength, FOREX.com analyst Fawad Razaqzada said in a note.

"Rising global bond yields suggest markets are increasingly prepared for the Fed and other central banks to push interest rates higher in their efforts to bring inflation back towards target," Razaqzada wrote, adding that higher real yields are particularly damaging for non-yielding assets such as gold.

"More generally, commodities have seen a wide-ranging selloff, particularly in metals, as volatility in AI valuations raises doubts about longer-term demand for copper or other data center capital inputs," MUFG's Soojin Kim said.

On Thursday, front-month Comex gold for November delivery fell 1.4% to $3,682.10/oz, and front-month Comex November silver slipped 1.5% to $44.318/oz, the lowest settlement for the respective metals since September 19 and 24, 2025.

data.title: Old Navy's Denim Brings Back Lower Earning Shoppers — Market Talk

data.title: BILL Agrees to be Acquired by TPG in Partnership with Corpay
data.description:
BILL (), the intelligent finance platform trusted by nearly 500,000 businesses to manage, move, and maximize their money, today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by TPG, a leading global alternative asset management firm, in partnership with Corpay (), the Global Spend Management Company. BILL will be acquired for $63.25 per share in a cash transaction that values BILL at $6.0 billion. TPG will acquire a majority interest in BILL through TPG Capital, the firm’s U.S. and European private equity platform, and Corpay will acquire a minority interest.

The per share purchase price represents a 31% premium to the 60-day volume-weighted average price ending on November 16, the last full trading day preceding media reports that BILL was in acquisition discussions.

“This transaction marks an exciting new chapter for BILL, delivering significant, certain, and immediate value to our stockholders, while creating new opportunities to accelerate our transformation and deliver greater value to customers,” said René Lacerte, CEO and Founder of BILL. “With our new partners, we will have the resources, expertise, and strategic support to accelerate innovation, advance our AI transformation, and continue to drive the future of financial operations. We look forward to the opportunities ahead for our customers and our business.”

“BILL has built a differentiated financial operations platform that helps small and midsize businesses manage their most critical financial workflows. We have long recognized the significant opportunity at the intersection of financial technology, AI, and payments, and believe BILL is well positioned to capitalize on these trends through its scaled network, integrated technology, and deep customer relationships,” said John Flynn, Partner at TPG. “We are excited to partner with the BILL team, combining TPG’s technology investing and business-building experience with Corpay’s payments expertise to accelerate innovation and support the company's next chapter,” added Tim Millikin, Partner at TPG.

“We’re excited about the potential this agreement represents and have great respect for everything the BILL team has accomplished. We see clear opportunities to support and complement BILL’s product roadmap, platform capabilities, and the services it offers to a broader range of customers. We look forward to working with BILL to further enhance its market-leading platform to deliver greater innovation and value to customers,” said Ron Clarke, Chairman and CEO of Corpay.

Transaction Details
The transaction, which was approved unanimously by the BILL Board of Directors, is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions, including approval by BILL stockholders and the receipt of required regulatory approvals. There are no financing conditions to the transaction. Starboard Value, BILL's largest stockholder, and BILL’s CEO and Founder, René Lacerte, have agreed to vote their shares in favor of the agreement.

Upon the close of the transaction, Mr. Lacerte will continue to lead BILL as CEO. BILL will become a privately held company, and its common stock will no longer be listed on any public stock exchange.

Advisors
Goldman Sachs and Qatalyst Partners are serving as financial advisors to BILL, Fenwick & West LLP is serving as BILL’s legal advisor, and Joele Frank, Wilkinson Brimmer Katcher is serving as strategic communications advisor.

BofA Securities, Inc., Deutsche Bank Securities Inc., and RBC Capital Markets, LLC are serving as financial advisors to TPG. Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP is serving as legal counsel.

Barclays is serving as financial adviser to Corpay. Sullivan & Cromwell LLP is serving as legal counsel.

About BILL
BILL () is the intelligent finance platform trusted by nearly half a million businesses and their accountants to manage, move, and maximize their money. BILL powers businesses ranging from fast-moving startups to growing companies with complex operations. We use AI to deliver strategic finance capabilities in one integrated platform that includes AP, AR, expenses, forecasting, procurement and more. With a member network of more than 9 million, BILL’s platform processes over 1% of US GDP annually. Headquartered in San Jose, California, BILL is a trusted partner of leading U.S. financial institutions, accounting firms, and software providers. For more information, visit bill.com.

About TPG
TPG is a leading global alternative asset management firm, founded in San Francisco in 1992, with $346 billion of assets under management and investment and operational teams around the world. TPG invests across a broadly diversified set of strategies, including private equity, impact, credit, real estate, and market solutions, and our unique strategy is driven by collaboration, innovation, and inclusion. Our teams combine deep product and sector experience with broad capabilities and expertise to develop differentiated insights and add value for our fund investors, portfolio companies, management teams, and communities.

About Corpay
Corpay (), the Global Spend Management Company, is an S&P 500 company with three primary B2B solution sets. Spend Management, provides corporate and virtual card programs and AP automation solutions. Cross-Border, helps businesses manage foreign-currency exposure and provides global multi-currency account solutions. Vehicle Solutions, controls fuel, tolls, parking and related vehicle spend. With Corpay, the more a business controls, the less it spends. To learn more, visit corpay.com.

Additional Information and Where to Find It
This communication may be deemed to be solicitation material in respect of the proposed transaction involving BILL Holdings, Inc. (“BILL”) and affiliates of TPG. In connection with the proposed transaction, BILL intends to file a preliminary proxy statement and a definitive proxy statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) with respect to a special meeting of stockholders to be held in connection with the proposed transaction. After filing the definitive proxy statement (the “Proxy Statement”) with the SEC, BILL will mail the Proxy Statement and a proxy card to each stockholder of BILL entitled to vote at the special meeting. This communication is not a substitute for the Proxy Statement or any other document that BILL may file with the SEC or send to its stockholders in connection with the proposed transaction. The Proxy Statement will contain important information about the proposed transaction and related matters. The Proxy Statement and other relevant materials filed or to be filed with the SEC will be made available to BILL’s investors and stockholders at no expense to them and copies may be obtained free of charge on BILL’s website at https://investor.bill.com/. In addition, all of those materials will be available at no charge on the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov.

Participants in the Solicitation
BILL and its directors, executive officers, other members of its management and employees may be deemed to be participants in the solicitation of proxies of BILL stockholders in connection with the proposed transaction under SEC rules. Investors and stockholders may obtain more detailed information regarding the names, affiliations and interests of BILL’s executive officers and directors in the solicitation by reading BILL’s definitive proxy statement for its 2026 annual meeting of stockholders, the Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 and the subsequent Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, SEC filings on Forms 3 and 4 by such directors and executive officers and the Proxy Statement and other relevant materials that will be filed with the SEC in connection with the proposed transaction when they become available. Any changes in the holdings of BILL’s securities by its directors or executive officers from the amounts described in BILL’s definitive proxy statement for its 2026 annual meeting of stockholders have been or will be reflected in Statements of Changes in Beneficial Ownership on Form 4 filed with the SEC subsequent to the filing date of BILL’s definitive proxy statement for its 2026 annual meeting of stockholders. Such filings are or will be available on the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov. Additional information regarding the identity of potential participants, and their direct or indirect interests, by security holdings or otherwise, will be included in the Proxy Statement when it is filed with the SEC. data.title: Japan Inflation Data Due On Friday
data.description:
HONG KONG (dpa-AFX) - Japan will on Friday release October figures for consumer prices, highlighting a modest day for Asia-Pacific economic activity.

Overall national inflation was flat on month and up 2.1 percent on year in September, while core CPI also rose an annual 2.1 percent.

New Zealand will provide October numbers for credit card spending; in September, spending was up 6.9 percent on year.

Malaysia will see October figures for imports, exports and trade balance. In September, imports were up 52.7 percent on year and exports rose an annual 545 percent for a trade surplus of MYR33.70 billion.

Taiwan will provide October data for export orders and Q3 numbers for current account. In September, export orders surged 62.4 percent on year, while the current account showed a surplus of $58.49 billion in Q2.

Hong Kong will release October figures for consumer prices; in September, overall inflation was up 0.3 percent on month and 1.9 percent on year.

data.title: Keysight Technologies Reports Strong Q4 Net Income Growth
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Keysight Technologies, Inc. (KEYS) on Thursday, reported a sharp increase in net income for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, supported by stronger revenue and a substantial rise in customer orders compared with the prior-year quarter.

Net income climbed to $486 million from $233 million in the three months ended October 31, 2025. Earnings per share increased to $2.82 from $1.35. Revenue advanced 40.5 percent to $1.994 billion from $1.419 billion, while orders surged to $2.339 billion from $1.533 billion.

For the full fiscal year, net income rose to $1.513 billion from $850 million, while revenue increased to $7.157 billion from $5.375 billion. Annual earnings per share reached $8.75, compared with $4.91 a year earlier.

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Keysight expects revenue of $2.040 billion to $2.060 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $3.63 to $3.69.

KEYS is currently trading after hours at $284.98, up $3.56 or 1.27 percent on the New York Stock Exchange.

data.title: California AG subpoenas Nvidia over concerns about former CEO, China ties
data.description:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta said on Thursday his office had served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia related to reports of former CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese spy.

"The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags," Bonta said, adding that his office was investigating whether China obtained Nvidia's advanced chips or confidential information, and if the company misled investors.

The probe will help determine whether Nvidia's actions violated California law, the attorney general's office said.

Huang resigned last week after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two with Nvidia employees.

data.title: Post Holdings 4Q Sales Slide on Broad Declines Across Categories
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Post Holdings reported a drop in quarterly sales on broad declines across several categories including cereal, pet food and egg products.

The maker of Honey Bunches of Oats and Nature's Recipe on Thursday posted a fourth-quarter profit of $81.8 million, or $1.68 a share, up from $58 million, or 99 cents a share, a year earlier.

Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted earnings per share were $1.84, ahead of the $1.78 per share expected by analysts, according to FactSet.

Sales fell 13% to $1.96 billion, below Wall Street expectations of $2 billion.

Post's shares were down slightly following the results in after hours trading, declining 1.53% to $79.28. The stock has tumbled 20% this year.

Sales from consumer brands, which consists of cereal, pet food and nutter butters, were down 15% at $989.6 million.

Foodservice, which includes egg and potato products, fell 12% to $635.2 million. Sales were also down for the company's refrigerated retail and Weetabix units.

For the current fiscal year, Post Holdings said it expects adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $1.45 billion and $1.5 billion. The company expects full-year capital expenditures from $360 million to $400 million.

Separately, Post Holdings named director Jeff Zadoks as interim chairman and said Chief Executive Nicolas Catoggio will assume full executive leadership while Executive Chairman Robert Vitale is on leave.

Post Holdings also named Christopher Growe and Nicholas Stiritz as board members, effective Dec.1.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com.

data.title: PanGenomic Health Announces Exclusive Distributorship Agreement with Colombian Subsidiary of Ayla Bioscience and Expiration of Non-Binding Letter of Intent
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

    Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, November 19, 2026 – TheNewswire - PanGenomic Health Inc. (“PanGenomic Health” or the “Company”) (CSE: NARA, FSE:LL3) announces that it is has signed an exclusive distributorship agreement (the “Distributorship Agreement”) with Colombia-based Zeotech Group S.A.S. (“Zeotech”), a wholly-owned subsidiary of US-based Ayla Bioscience Inc.

    Under the terms of the Distributorship Agreement, PanGenomic Health will have the right to market and sell a range of natural health products made by Zeotech from its production facility in Bogota, Colombia.  The products include Zeofoodz, a line of high-nutrition functional

    foods, Zeophytoz, a line of high-quality botanical extracts and resins, and Zeomycel, a line of functional mushrooms.  All products are made from natural ingredients sourced in the Andean and Amazon basins of South America, and dehydrated using Zeotech’s patented technologies that avoid affecting molecular structure and biological activity.

    PanGenomic Health will have an initial one year period of exclusivity in Canada to market and sell the Zeotech products, and the Company plans to market the private-labelled products online through its Agenta ecommerce platform and through natural health retail partners.

    The Company further announced that it is no longer pursuing the proposed business combination transaction with Ayla Bioscience Inc., as previously announced on April 14, 2026.  PanGenomic Health’s non-binding Letter of Intent with Ayla Bioscience has expired in accordance with its terms.  PanGenomic Health will continue to explore partnership opportunities to create a broad suite of products that provide consumers and health practitioners with access to personalized medicine tools and sustainable, high-value natural products.

    About PanGenomic Health

data.title: A CoreWeave co-founder just made an unconventional $30 million wager on its battered bonds
data.description:
By Christine Ji

While executives typically buy shares to signal confidence, CoreWeave co-founder Brian Venturo is turning to the bond market to calm AI jitters

CoreWeave's 9.75% senior unsecured notes have recently traded around 81 cents on the dollar.

As CoreWeave faces concerns about its debt load and financial profile, one of its co-founders is responding with an unusual move.

CoreWeave (CRWV) co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer Brian Venturo shared in a LinkedIn post Wednesday that he had purchased $30 million in face value of the company's unsecured bonds, which he intends to hold until maturity on Oct. 1, 2031.

"I've never been more confident in CoreWeave," he wrote. The company shared his statement in a social-media post on X.

Venturo's recent move was initially well received by investors, with CoreWeave shares rising as much as 10.5% Thursday. They've since turned negative amid broader pressure on the technology sector, and they're down nearly 50% since the beginning of October.

The SEC mandates that executives must file a public Form 4 within two business days whenever they buy or sell company stock or convertible bonds that can turn into stock. But no such rule applies to regular, nonconvertible bonds, meaning that the market didn't have knowledge of Venturo's purchase until he posted about it.

Insider purchases like Venturo's can signal management confidence in a company, although purchases of stock are far more typical. Executives who believe their company is undervalued can receive much more upside by buying stock. High-profile past examples of executives holding debt have usually been more extreme cases of downside protection. Former Sears CEO Eddie Lampert extended over $2.6 billion in loans to the struggling retailer through his hedge fund ahead of its 2018 bankruptcy.

Some commentators on social media also pointed out that Venturo had recently sold shares of CoreWeave. According to an SEC filing, he sold over 80,000 shares of the company in the three months ending Sept. 30.

CoreWeave declined to comment.

Both CoreWeave's debt and equity have sold off due to artificial-intelligence jitters in recent months. The company's business model currently depends heavily on bringing data centers online with borrowed money, leaving it exposed to rising interest rates or slowdowns in demand for AI processing power. The bond series matching the maturity date that Venturo gave are CoreWeave's 9.75% senior unsecured notes, meaning that they aren't backed by company assets. These notes recently traded at roughly 81 cents on the dollar, according to LSEG.

CoreWeave had already taken steps to mitigate Wall Street's concerns, announcing during its recent third-quarter earnings call that it doesn't intend to tap the unsecured debt market for funding at current yields. Instead, the company said it will utilize customer prepayments and delay-draw term loans - facilities backed by specific customer contracts that allow it to borrow money in installments.

-Christine Ji

data.title: Bitcoin slides toward $60,000 as spot ETF outflows near $3 billion
data.description:
Bitcoin is having a rough November. On Thursday, November 19, the largest crypto asset traded at approximately $63,800 after a week that took about 13% off its price.

The slide has put the psychologically important $60,000 mark within view.

Three forces are doing the damage at once: steady money leaving US spot Bitcoin ETFs, a broad sell-off on Wall Street, and growing worry that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates again.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw about $2.9 billion in net outflows for November through the 18th. That figure covers fewer than three weeks of trading.

The pace picked up toward the end of that stretch. Daily outflows came in at $239.9 million on November 17, then climbed to between $306.4 million and $306.5 million on November 18.

One name stands out. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, ticker IBIT, accounted for approximately 83% to 87% of the month's ETF outflows.

The cumulative result shows up on the balance sheet. Combined net assets across the Bitcoin ETFs fell to $77.7 billion, a three-month low.

The ETF story is not happening in isolation. Crypto losses on Thursday came alongside a wide sell-off in traditional markets, as risk assets broadly lost favor.

Concerns about further Federal Reserve rate hikes are a big part of that mood.

Rising Treasury yields and a strong dollar have piled on. Those conditions helped push Bitcoin to roughly 20% below the average entry prices set during recent institutional purchases.

Intraday action reflected the stress. Bitcoin dipped below $63,000 at points, and earlier in the week it touched a 24-hour low of $62,068.

Another source of supply is coming from inside the industry. Mining companies including Riot and Marathon Digital (MARA) have liquidated assets to fund new AI infrastructure, which has added to selling pressure.

For anyone tracking institutional demand, the ETF data is the most important signal on the board. Nearly $3 billion leaving in under three weeks shows that bridge carries traffic in both directions.

The concentration in IBIT matters as well. When one fund drives the vast majority of redemptions, it points to a specific set of holders reshaping their exposure, rather than a slow drift across the entire market.

The gap between current prices and recent institutional entry points is a second risk. With Bitcoin around 20% below where many large buyers got in, a further decline could test the conviction of those holders and invite more selling.

The $60,000 level is the obvious marker to watch. Daily ETF flow data is the other key indicator. A slowdown in redemptions, or a return to inflows, would be the first sign that institutional demand is stabilizing.

Bitcoin has shed about 13% in a week, institutional buyers are underwater, and the macro backdrop is offering little help.

data.title: Marsh to Highlight How Perspective Drives Performance at the Formula 1® Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix
data.description:
Marsh (), the leading professional services firm in risk, strategy, people, and investments, will have a prominent presence at the Formula 1® Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix as Formula 1's Official Risk Partner and Official Insurance Brokering Partner. During the event, taking place November 19–21, 2026 on the streets of Las Vegas, Marsh will have trackside signage and out of home advertising throughout the street circuit.

The Las Vegas Grand Prix — now in its third year since debuting in 2023 — drew approximately 56 million viewers worldwide last year and runs on the second-longest street circuit in the 2026 season at 6.201 kilometers. The race is one of eight street circuits on the calendar this year, and its Las Vegas Strip setting makes it among the most recognizable events in the global sport.

"The Las Vegas Grand Prix is one of the most watched sporting events on the planet, and it gives us a remarkable stage to bring our clients into the center of that energy," said John Jones, Chief Marketing and Communications Officer at Marsh. "Formula 1 attracts the kind of business leaders we work with every day — people who understand that performance, at its core, is about how you manage risk to seize opportunity and drive results. That's the conversation we're here to have."

The weekend will feature high-level engagement with Marsh, Formula 1 leadership and racing experts. Events include a fireside chat between Michelle Sartain, President of Marsh Risk US and Canada, and Emily Prazer, Chief Commercial Officer of Formula 1 and CEO of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, as well as a discussion between Kate Brennan, Marsh General Counsel, Stefano Domenicali, President and CEO of Formula 1, and Chris Medland, Formula 1 journalist and commentator. The events will offer Marsh clients a rare window into the strategic thinking driving one of the world's fastest-growing sports properties, as well as insights into making decisions under pressure and recognizing winning opportunities both on and off the track.

Marsh's presence at Las Vegas is part of its broader activation across the 2026 Formula 1 season, which includes trackside branding at select races and The Risk Perspective, a content series featured on F1.com and the F1 app. The series explores specific circuits where drivers and teams must interpret risk, adapt to evolving conditions, and make decisive calls under pressure — illustrating how perspective turns uncertainty into advantage and insight into performance.

Marsh, across its businesses, has a long history of working closely with leading companies in the automotive, transportation, mobility, sports, and entertainment sectors. The Formula 1 partnership enables Marsh to engage more deeply with clients and industry stakeholders worldwide, showcasing tailored solutions that respond to evolving risks and opportunities.

Marsh () is a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. With annual revenue of $27 billion and more than 95,000 colleagues, Marsh helps build the confidence to thrive through the power of perspective. data.title: Anthropic's $81 Bln IPO Highlights AI's Trillion-Dollar Potential
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Anthropic (ANT) has made history with an $81.3 billion initial public offering, becoming the first publicly traded frontier artificial intelligence company and reaching a fully diluted valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion.

The maker of the Claude chatbot priced its shares at $83 apiece, above its marketed range of $70 to $78, reflecting strong investor demand.

Its Nasdaq debut on November 19 under the ticker ANT saw shares open at $111.50, approximately 34.3 percent above the IPO price, briefly pushing its market valuation beyond $2 trillion. The offering surpassed SpaceX's $75 billion IPO in June 2026 to become the largest in history.

Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers Dario and Daniela Amodei, Anthropic has emerged as a major player in the AI industry. Its Claude models power chatbot, coding and enterprise applications, generating revenue through consumption-based services and paid subscriptions.

Revenue surged to $4.59 billion in 2025 from $386 million in 2024. First-half 2026 revenue reached $16.29 billion, compared with $1.16 billion a year earlier. Meanwhile, its operating loss narrowed to $693 million from $2.14 billion, indicating improving financial performance.

However, sustaining this growth requires substantial investment. Anthropic has committed more than $600 billion in spending with approximately eight partners over a decade, including at least $110 billion with Amazon, $114.5 billion with Google and $44.9 billion with Microsoft. Amazon and Google are also major investors, highlighting the interconnected financial relationships underpinning the AI industry.

Competition from OpenAI, Google, Meta and other AI developers remain intense. Nevertheless, Anthropic has established a strong enterprise presence, accounting for 60.5 percent of AI token spending tracked by Ramp during the week ended October 23.

For investors, Anthropic offers exposure to the rapidly expanding AI market, supported by exceptional revenue growth and increasing enterprise adoption. However, its $1.5 trillion IPO valuation places considerable emphasis on future execution.

Its ability to manage infrastructure costs, maintain its competitive position and translate growing demand into sustainable profits will ultimately determine whether its market valuation is justified.
